title: Gate at a specified index
statement: Let $n,k,j$ be natural numbers and let $f$ be a Boolean function on strings of length $n$. The gate at index $j$ is a NOT gate reading input $j$ if $j<n$; otherwise it is selected from the heap-gate range when $j<z(n,k)$, from the function-gate range when $j<f(n,k)$, from the function-code gate range when $j<c(n,k)$, and from the combination-gate range thereafter, with the corresponding offsets and parameters determined by these ranges.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean-valued function on length-$n$ Boolean strings
caveat: The supplied snippet does not define `heapGate`, `funcGate`, or `combGate`, so their constructions and precise parameter meanings cannot be stated.
